summary: Launch-week mix. Mostly open-source swaps for paid tools (voice, chat, search, images, clips), plus Omnisend's MCP, the ECC skills toolkit and small AI-product launches. Free coding routing (FreeLLMAPI) and ECC are the most useful for Claude Code.

tools.name: Pexo
tools.what: AI video agent that turns an idea into a product launch video.
tools.shown: Hosts discussed it and showed the site; no live build.
tools.quote: It's an AI video agent that turns your ideas into videos.
tools.check: Pricing not stated.

opinion.why: Good for cheap or mini launch videos, or as the back end of a launch agency.
opinion.quote: you could use this tool to launch your products or to create launch videos.

our_view.for_what: One intro or channel-launch video to test it
our_view.why: They pitch it for product launches; Charlie has no product. Rule 42: try the simplest video route first.

tools.name: Spira AI
tools.what: Platform that creates and runs a fake AI influencer account promoting your product.
tools.shown: Showed an example AI influencer promoting a brand; hosts did not try it.
tools.quote: you can now get your own fake influencer that's basically just promoting your stuff.
tools.check: 50% off offer claimed; Product Hunt number one claim not verified.

opinion.why: Host finds it fun and effective but wouldn't use it; Corey says skip it and you get left behind.
opinion.quote: I don't know that I would mess with this, but I do think it looks like it's fun and it's super effective.

our_view.why: A fake face on a channel about learning in public is off-brand; Rule 37 (check before anything goes public). We side with the host, not the 'left behind' push.

tools.name: ChatGPT Dots
tools.what: OpenAI agent that can manage Codex threads and ChatGPT chats from one place.
tools.shown: Corey described using it as a chief of staff to spin up and track Codex threads; Andrew found it nagging.
tools.quote: I use Dot as almost the manager of codec.
tools.check: Availability and price not stated.

opinion.why: Corey uses it as a chief of staff for Codex threads; the host only gets nagging.
opinion.quote: I use Dot as almost the manager of codec.

our_view.for_what: Only if Codex threads pile up too many to track
our_view.why: Split verdict is fair. Rule 43: test it on Charlie's own tasks before switching; Rule 42: no manager layer until the pain shows.

tools.name: Hark
tools.what: New agent app with better web browser access and widgets that track your accounts.
tools.shown: Showed Alex Finn's screenshot of widgets; hosts were lukewarm and had not used it.
tools.quote: I don't see it being that unique enough for me to go and test it out
tools.check: Early access; price unknown.

opinion.why: Not unique enough to replace Dots or other agents.
opinion.quote: I don't see it being that unique enough for me to go and test it out

our_view.why: Early access, nothing shown working. Rule 42: adopt tools only for real pain.

tools.name: Claude for Startups
tools.what: Anthropic programme giving eligible startups a year of Claude for Teams and API credits.
tools.shown: Read out the offer; hosts said they are applying.
tools.quote: free access. One year of Claude for Teams, $1,000 in Claude API credits
tools.check: Official FAQ checked 2026-10-09: free Team/$1,000 credit offers currently over capacity. Eligibility, approval and usable credits are unverified; do not present as immediately available. https://claude.com/programs/startups

opinion.why: Free year of Claude for Teams plus API credits is a no-brainer to apply for.
opinion.quote: I think it's a no-brainer. Like, why not go and apply?

our_view.for_what: Free credits for the channel, if it counts as a startup
our_view.why: Applying costs nothing, but check UK eligibility and the terms first. A sign-up goes on the Decision Desk.

cost.amount: 1 year of Claude for Teams + $1,000 API credits, if eligible

tools.name: Instinct
tools.what: Personal AI agent that lives in iMessage and just added group chats.
tools.shown: Corey described finding accountant documents in his email within about 60 seconds by text.
tools.quote: So, it has access to my email.
tools.check: Needs email and card access; check privacy. Price not stated.

opinion.why: Finds accountant documents in his email in about a minute by text.
opinion.quote: it found it within like 60 seconds.

our_view.why: Needs email and card access. Rule 36: permissions in layers, read-only first; this repo is public, so no private data near it.

cost.amount: free for now (until its funding is settled)

tools.name: VMPal
tools.what: Mac app that runs isolated virtual machines so an agent gets its own computer.
tools.shown: Andrew explained plans to run a fresh Mac OS VM for agents; no demo.
tools.quote: if you're going to give your agent a computer, you might as well put it on your own computer and then isolate it to that one computer.
tools.check: One-off fee of about $34-35 claimed; Mac only as described.

opinion.why: A cheap one-off fee for a clean Mac with agents isolated on it.
opinion.quote: This one is the app that I'm going to rebuild my whole MacBook around.

our_view.why: Mac only and a lot of set-up for a beginner. Rule 42: lowest rung first; cloud sessions are already isolated.

tools.name: Boring Funnels
tools.what: Weekly full-funnel breakdowns plus a copy-able prompt for Claude Code or Codex to rebuild the funnel.
tools.shown: Described the product; no live use.
tools.quote: one-click prompt that you can one-click copy, hand to Claude Code, or hand to Codex
tools.check: Price said as '$2.99 a year' in captions; verify.

opinion.why: Copy-and-hand-to-Claude funnel prompts, and a possible agency back end.
opinion.quote: this is such a no-brainer.

our_view.why: Charlie has no funnels to rebuild. Rule 39: adopt tools only for real pain. Check the '$2.99 a year' price.

cost.amount: said as '$2.99 a year' (probably a caption slip; check)

tools.name: Skillry
tools.what: Paid directory of premium agent skills with a visible demo of each output.
tools.shown: Showed the site, a pixel promo video skill demo and its verified revenue.
tools.quote: This is where you pay a smaller price for premium skills and you can see exactly what the output's going to look like before you buy it.
tools.check: $5,000 a month revenue claim via TrustMRR; skill price $4.99 as stated.

opinion.why: Praises paid skills with a visible demo as a business idea; doesn't say they'd buy one.
opinion.quote: This is where you pay a smaller price for premium skills and you can see exactly what the output's going to look like before you buy it.

our_view.why: Rule 34: a skill earns its place when built from a real run. Rule 37: vet any bought skill before installing.

cost.amount: monthly fee, or buy all; single skills from $4.99

tools.name: CreativeClaw
tools.what: One MCP that adds image, video and voiceover generation to Claude, Codex and other agents, pay per use.
tools.shown: Showed example outputs and revenue page.
tools.quote: with one MCP, you get to make it into much more of an artist.
tools.check: Revenue figures ($10k MRR, $125k lifetime) are the founder's; verify.

opinion.why: One pay-per-use MCP beats several separate subscriptions.
opinion.quote: makes so much more sense than going to 11 Labs and paying for a subscription

our_view.for_what: Thumbnails and voiceover for the channel
our_view.why: Pay-per-use fits a beginner. Rule 43: compare one thumbnail with his current route first; Rule 37: vet the MCP before installing.

tools.name: vibe-code.ing
tools.what: Clean single-page directory of AI tools, monetised by sponsored spots.
tools.shown: Showed the site as an example of a simple profitable idea.
tools.quote: this is just a really good example of a AI tool directory done right.
tools.check: Sponsored slot price stated as about $350.

opinion.why: A clean one-page directory he would return to for design tools.
opinion.quote: this is just a really good example of a AI tool directory done right.

our_view.why: The Hands Brain already is our tool directory. Interesting idea only if the site went public (Rule 37 first).

tools.name: TinyPopups
tools.what: Embeddable website popup widget with triggers, installed in about five minutes.
tools.shown: Described the features and claimed reply rates; no demo.
tools.quote: intelligent website popups that take five it takes 5 minutes to install this on your website.
tools.check: 30% reply rate is the maker's claim.

opinion.why: Simple five-minute popups for people who don't want to code.
opinion.quote: be a customer of this for sure.

our_view.why: Charlie has no website needing popups. The 30% reply rate is the maker's claim (Rule 43).

tools.name: Omnisend MCP
tools.what: MCP that lets Claude or another agent build email campaigns and customer segments in Omnisend.
tools.shown: Live demo in Claude: campaign draft from top campaigns, new-subscriber segment, competitor style guide from Gmail, then a campaign.
tools.quote: Based on the best performing email campaigns, I want you to use Omnisend MCP to create an email campaign
tools.check: Sponsor link with 30% off; pricing and free tier not stated. Image upload through Claude failed in demo.

opinion.why: Would drive campaigns and segments from his agent, but keeps multi-step automations inside Omnisend.
opinion.quote: I know that it's faster to be inside on this end, but I still think I would use my agent.

our_view.why: Needs an Omnisend store and a mailing list; Charlie has neither. Sponsor link in the video. Rule 39: adopt a tool only for real pain.

tools.name: VoiceStudio
tools.what: Free desktop app for voice cloning, text-to-speech and video dubbing, run locally.
tools.shown: Played sample voices and the install page.
tools.quote: There is no credit counter, so you can redo a line 50 times and it's going to cost you nothing.
tools.check: Default model is non-commercial only; Pro is $99 a month.

opinion.why: Free, no credit meter, so retries cost nothing; a little nervous about copying voices.
opinion.quote: There is no credit counter, so you can redo a line 50 times and it's going to cost you nothing. That's why I'm so excited about this.

our_view.for_what: Free voiceover for channel videos, if Charlie ever wants a voice other than his own
our_view.why: His excitement is about saving credits Charlie does not pay for. Rule 39 (real pain only); Rule 37: no cloning anyone's voice, and this repo is public.

tools.name: Odysseus
tools.what: Private ChatGPT-style assistant on your computer with local models, memory, research and agents, made by PewDiePie.
tools.shown: Described features and the GitHub repo; no demo.
tools.quote: you're going to get chat, you're going to get deep research, you're going to get memory
tools.check: Host says it is not as good as ChatGPT.

opinion.why: Private and free, but he says plainly it is no ChatGPT replacement.
opinion.quote: I'm also going to tell you it's really not as good as Chat GPT.

our_view.why: Charlie already has Claude Code and Codex; a weaker local chat adds a tool without removing a pain. Rule 42: lowest rung that works.

tools.name: FreeLLMAPI
tools.what: Routes a coding agent across many free model providers so you can keep coding when one hits its limit.
tools.shown: Explained the idea and said the install is easy; no coding demo.
tools.quote: string together all these freebies
tools.check: Does not include Claude or frontier models; optional $19 a year add-on. Host frames it as replacing Claude Code for some people.

opinion.why: Easiest install on the list; he says it was one of the first things he did when limits bit.
opinion.quote: this is the easiest install probably on the list

our_view.for_what: A fallback if Claude Code usage limits stop a session
our_view.why: He is a heavy user who hits caps; Charlie may not. It sends code to free third-party providers and excludes Claude, so Rule 43 (test on his own work) and Rule 26 (keys stay in .env) come first.

tools.name: Vane
tools.what: Self-hosted research assistant that searches the web and gives numbered sources; formerly Perplexica.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: You type a question. It searches the web. It writes the answer. It gives you numbered sources.
tools.check: Host says it is not as strong as Perplexity; needs a model (Ollama or free Gemini key).

opinion.why: Free, cited answers, but he doubts it matches Perplexity.
opinion.quote: I don't think it's nearly as strong as Perplexity for many people.

our_view.why: Claude Code already searches the web with sources; a self-hosted search app needs a model and setup. Rule 42.

tools.name: InvokeAI
tools.what: Open-source local image studio with layered canvas and editing.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: It's the AI image studio that you can run yourself.
tools.check: Needs a strong GPU or recent Mac.

opinion.why: Calls it phenomenal but warns it needs a gaming graphics card or a recent Mac.
opinion.quote: This thing is phenomenal.

our_view.why: Strong hardware needed and no image pain today. Thumbnails can start with the simplest route first (Rule 42).

tools.name: ACE-Step
tools.what: Open-source song generator with vocals that runs on your own computer.
tools.shown: Made a short hip-hop song on the hosted web version; host said it was not as good as Suno.
tools.quote: unlimited songs hosted by you for free.
tools.check: Quality below Suno per host.

opinion.why: Free and unlimited, but he tried it and was underwhelmed against Suno.
opinion.quote: I don't think it's anything to write home about.

our_view.for_what: Free background music for channel videos
our_view.why: His own test was weak, so try the hosted version on one real video before any install (Rule 43).

tools.name: OpenShorts
tools.what: Self-hosted tool that turns long videos into captioned vertical clips and can schedule posts.
tools.shown: Ran it on a YouTube video on the free hosted site; framing needed fixing.
tools.quote: This is a free clip maker that you can host yourself or you can go to their website and use for free.
tools.check: Hosted free tier is 20 minutes a month with watermark; self-hosting slow without GPU.

opinion.why: Free hosted clip maker, but his test clip was badly framed and needed manual fixing.
opinion.quote: I have to go into edit framing and then I go and I reframe it.

our_view.for_what: Cutting Shorts from Charlie's own videos once the channel has long videos
our_view.why: Try the free hosted tier (20 minutes a month, watermark) on one real video first; do not self-host. Rules 42 and 43.

vs.gap: Cuts long videos into vertical clips, where HyperFrames makes new motion graphics; untested until Charlie has a long video to cut.

tools.name: Dyad
tools.what: Open-source local app builder that turns plain English into apps using your chosen AI model.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: You just describe what you want in plain English and you get it.
tools.check: Model cost depends on what you plug in; free Gemini key possible.

opinion.why: Describes it, then doubts it will last because Claude Code does the same job.
opinion.quote: maybe even this is uh is a tool whose days are numbered because we're seeing more and more that claude code can do this stuff on its own.

our_view.why: Charlie already builds in Claude Code, so a second app builder is a duplicate. Rule 42; reuse before building (capability map).

tools.name: OpenManus
tools.what: Open-source general agent that plans, browses, codes and saves files using your own model.
tools.shown: Described features; no demo.
tools.quote: You type what you want, the goal in English, and it plans the steps itself.
tools.check: Needs a paid API key or limited free tier.

opinion.why: Describes it and flags the paid model cost; never says he would use it.

our_view.why: Needs a paid API key, and Claude Code plus Codex already plan and act on goals. Rule 39.

tools.name: Upscayl
tools.what: Free desktop app that upscales photos four times locally, singly or in bulk.
tools.shown: Showed the repo and described the models.
tools.quote: It runs on your computer so your photos never leave
tools.check: Needs a Vulkan-capable GPU.

opinion.why: Recommends it for old, low-res photo folders; likes that photos stay on the computer.
opinion.quote: this is the tool for you.

our_view.why: His case is a folder of old photos; Charlie has none to rescue. Rule 39.

tools.name: ECC
tools.what: Open-source toolkit of skills that plans, builds with tests, makes a promo video and sends outreach.
tools.shown: Live 20-minute run: orchestrator drove tmux panes, built a pitch-roasting app, made a video, drafted and sent X DMs.
tools.quote: we're going to give it a task and build a product. So, it's going to use ECC skills
tools.check: Star count (271k) and exit claims are the guest's; X DM step needs private context and credentials.

opinion.why: Runs it himself and now mostly lets it run unwatched.
opinion.quote: most of the time I am very hands-off now um with the way I code

our_view.for_what: Borrow its plan and test-first skills for the OS, not the outreach
our_view.why: He is hands-off and had it DM real people from his accounts; Rule 36 says drafts first with a human approving outward actions, Rule 33 a separate checker, Rule 37 check before anything goes public.
